SddReadiness.keywords: readiness, setup, bootstrap, tooling, package-json, npm-scripts, gennady, stub, not-ready, proxy-handoff, sdd-readiness
SddReadiness.Mission:
Bring a not-ready repo to the point where the SDD flow can run: a `package.json` exists and declares the seven exact scripts `sdd-state` checks — `type-check` · `test` · `test:coverage` · `lint` (reaching `gennady`, read-only) · `format` (read-only) · `check` (read-only composite: `type-check` → `test` → `lint` → `format`) · `fix` (the one script allowed to write: `format:fix` → `lint:fix` → `check`) — gennady is installed, and `READINESS` flips to `ready`. This is the minimal mechanical bootstrap, NOT the tooling design: a real command where a tool is already installed, else a visible TODO stub that points at the infra flow. Entered when `sdd-state` reports `READINESS=not-ready` — from the router preflight or from any skill's own preflight. Self-sufficient: it may run without the router core in context, so it repeats the operator-facing axioms it needs.
Input — the `sdd-state` readiness verdict. Output — a `package.json` patched toward `ready`, plus a handed-over command list for anything that FAILED when the agent tried it (typically dependency installs the corporate proxy 403s).
Out of scope: choosing the real tool stack with a Decision Log (the infra branch), and the project portal (the root branch). This flow only makes the commands EXIST and runnable.
SddReadiness.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE
The SDD mechanical tools are `gennady` CLI commands. When working IN the gennady repo itself (including any worktree), the runner is `npx tsx /cli/gennady.ts`; in every other project it is `npx gennady`. Thus a Step's canonical `npx gennady ` fixes the command and arguments exactly; substitute only this runner when developing gennady itself, using the current worktree's root. Tools: `sdd-state`, `sdd-task`, `sdd-extract`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-log`, `sdd-sync`, `sdd-check`, `sdd-new`, `sdd-migrate`, `sdd-orient`, `sdd-session`, `orient`, `lint`, `yagni`, `testcov`. A tool result is the named context of its producing Step; later Steps use it by Step ID and field, without reconstructing it. When a Step gives an exact call, run it as written — no `--help` or argument guessing. Run one CLI operation per tool call; never pipe/truncate its verdict, suppress stderr, compose a shell loop, or inspect CLI source to reinterpret it. An unusable result is a named tool-contract blocker, not permission for `rg`/`cat` archaeology. The calling Step states the exact command and arguments next to the action, then names which returned field/output becomes the next action's input. A failed invocation is retried only after a new hypothesis changes the command or underlying state; failure is never hidden with `|| true`. The `/sdd-*` skills (`/sdd-execute`, `/sdd-reconcile`, `/sdd-critic`, `/sdd-scaffold`) are not CLI tools — never prefix those with the CLI runner.
Move forward unless stopped — gated by confidence and stakes: - HIGH confidence + low-stakes step → show the result and proceed; the operator can object at any moment. - LOW confidence, OR a high-stakes step (architecture, pivot, a trust boundary, an irreversible choice) → hard stop, wait for the operator.
The agent never closes a step it is unsure about, and never auto-agrees to a risky shortcut (see `AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`).
Named hard stops — Approval Checks and the SCALE confirmation exchange — are exempt from the proceed rule; they always stop, however high the confidence.
Keep the dialogue compact: no repeat questions; group obvious questions into one; on long dialogues show the delta, not a full restate. Confidence is `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` and lives in the dim service line, not narrated each round.
The agent's job is to protect the operator from their own blind spots and lead them to a sound decision — even a junior operator. - Warn, don't only ask: name the risk that will hurt later, the requirement likely missing, the thing probably forgotten, the trust boundary (auth, payments, persistence) that needs a real runtime. - Pull the thread, don't fill a quota: after each answer, check whether it opened a new gap or risk; if so, follow it until the gap is actually closed — not until a question count is hit. - Ask developing questions — ones that deepen the topic and check what should and should NOT exist — not merely uncomfortable ones. Never announce a question; just ask it plainly. - Neutral and critical: if the operator wants to skip something risky, surface the cost and ask for a reason; never silently agree.
Blind-spot instincts (not a checklist to recite): canonical source of truth? behavior on dependency failure? where simulation ends and real runtime begins? who validates input here? which assumption, if wrong, kills the design?
Every fix must be operator-approved before execution. The plan is shown as a table. No edits are made before explicit operator "yes" / "go" / "ok". Operator may edit the plan (remove items, change classification, add notes).
A recommendation must be the result of a search, not the first typical answer. Aligned models collapse to the modal option; a single quick recommendation usually IS that mode, which is rarely the best fit for a specific task.
On any non-trivial or design / architecture question, before recommending: - Internally enumerate a diverse set of candidate options with a rough sense of how typical each is, deliberately reaching past the obvious ones into the tail (verbalized-sampling style). - Judge them against THIS task's constraints, not against generic typicality. - Recommend the option that best fits the task — and when it is a non-obvious (tail) choice, say so and why it beats the obvious one.
Stakes gate the presentation (see `AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`): on a high-stakes / architecture question, present the strongest alternatives WITHOUT pre-anchoring a single pick, or pair the recommendation with the strongest alternative and the reason; on low-stakes, a direct recommendation is fine.
The operator never sees the agent's machinery. No «DIRECTIVE ACTIVATED», no mode-detection narration, no «grounding collected», no «перехожу к STEP_2», no frame-stack talk. Detection, reading, and step transitions happen silently. Mode / scope / confidence live in the dim service line and the log, nowhere else.
Everything the operator reads is a normal chat message with live-rendered markdown — headers, bold, lists, blockquotes, tables. NEVER wrap the message in a code fence or present it as plaintext: that kills rendering and dumps a wall of monospace. Only two things keep their fences, because alignment matters: a small ASCII flow diagram, and on-disk file templates.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
A question to the operator fires only through `AskUserQuestion` — or, when the tool is unavailable, a plain-text fallback carrying the same context plus an explicit list of named options — and always after the context is explained in the same message, never as bare free-form text. Batch mutually independent sub-questions into one call; dependent questions go one call at a time, composed only after the previous answer is in. No numbering, no semantic question IDs.
Full format, with worked examples — `QUESTION_FORMAT` in the interview / vision directives.

A halt is a plain sentence first (what happened + what to do), with the token as a trailing tag:
🛑 <что случилось по-человечески> — <что сделать оператору> `[H_*]`

SddReadiness.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_OPERATOR_REJECTS_SETUP` | Operator declines to set the project up. Without the required scripts no SDD branch can run — state that plainly and stop |

Step.Goal: State the honest readiness gap, straight from sdd-state.
Step.Action: Take everything from `sdd-state`'s `[READINESS]` block — `package.json` present/absent, each required script declared/not, `lint→gennady`, `check→read-only`, `gennady-installed` — plus the `missing` list (which now names `format(read-only)` and `lint(read-only)` separately from `check(read-only)` when a formatter/linter write switch leaks into that script's own chain). That tool is the single source of state (`AX_TOOL_INVOCATION`); do not re-derive it by hand. Tell the operator, in plain Russian (`AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`), exactly what is present and what is missing. No narration, just the gap. Flow into the plan (no STOP).

Step.Goal: Lay out the fix and get a go-ahead.
Step.Action: From the `missing` list, lay out what will be done: patch `package.json` (real command where the tool is already a dependency, else a TODO stub), wire `lint` to `gennady`, keep `format` / `lint` / `check` read-only (any formatter/linter write switch moves to `format:fix` / `lint:fix`, called only from `fix`), and install the missing dependencies / `gennady`. If the operator wants to lock a real tool now (test runner, formatter, type-checker) — a genuine NEW pick, not the stub path — run a research gate first: 2–3 targeted WebSearch queries (is each candidate alive and current, how AI-agent-friendly it is this year — text-configurable, autofix, machine-readable diagnostics) before offering 2–3 options with trade-offs (`AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`); for each option, one line on why it's offered per the research (not recall) plus the source. If WebSearch is unavailable here, say so plainly — `предлагаю по памяти на <дата обучения модели>, ресёрч недоступен` — a named caveat, not silence. Otherwise stub it and defer the choice to the infra flow (no research needed for a stub). Present the plan + Approval Check (`AX_OPERATOR_AGREEMENT` — no edits before an explicit go-ahead). STOP.

Step.Goal: Do everything the agent can — edits and installs.
Step.Action: With approval: create `package.json` if absent (name + `scripts`); add the seven exact scripts — real command where the tool exists, else the TODO stub (see Reference Data); `lint` always reaches `gennady`; `format` / `lint` / `check` stay read-only — any write switch (`--fix`, `--write`) goes only in `format:fix` / `lint:fix`, which `fix` chains into `check`; AND run the dependency installs the project needs (`npm i -D …`, gennady) — try them — the corporate proxy often blocks installs, but not always. Re-run `sdd-state`. Anything that failed goes to STEP_3.

Step.Goal: Report any failed command and hand it to the operator — once, no loop.
Step.Action: For each command that FAILED in STEP_2 (typically an install the proxy 403'd), immediately tell the operator the EXACT command that did not work and the error — once, no retry, no environment-fixing. Hand it over to run themselves. Present the failed-command block and wait (`HALT_FORMAT`-style). STOP until the operator runs them and says done («готово / дальше»).

WHEN `STEP_3_REPORT_FAILURES` ran (some command failed and the operator stepped in by hand) → re-run `sdd-state` now — the operator's own actions changed state since STEP_2's snapshot, so it is stale. WHEN `STEP_3` was skipped (STEP_2 applied cleanly, nothing failed) → reuse STEP_2's own closing `sdd-state` re-run directly; it is already the fresh post-apply snapshot, and a second call here would just re-confirm it — a wasted turn. Either way: `READINESS=ready` → setup is done; return control to the caller (the router's classify/route step, or the skill's own flow). Still `not-ready` → state the remaining gap and resume at `STEP_1` for the leftover items only — a fresh assessment, never a blind re-run of a command that already failed.

SddReadiness.ReferenceData:
The seven exact script names `sdd-state` checks (exact match — `type-check` also accepts the `typecheck` spelling, every other name has exactly one):
| script | purpose | stubbable until infra flow? | |---|---|---| | `type-check` | type-check, no emit | yes | | `test` | run tests | yes | | `test:coverage` | tests with coverage | yes | | `lint` | lint chain that reaches `gennady` (DbC), read-only | **no — must wire gennady** | | `format` | formatter in check-only mode — read-only | yes | | `check` | read-only composite: `type-check` → `test` → `lint` → `format` | no — wire the chain | | `fix` | the one script allowed to write: `format:fix` → `lint:fix` → `check` | no — wire the chain |
`format`, `lint`, and `check` — and every script any of them reaches via `npm run ` — must stay free of known write switches (`eslint … --fix`, `prettier … --write`); a leaked write switch fails that script's own read-only check (`format(read-only)` / `lint(read-only)` / `check(read-only)` in `missing`), even if every script name is present. Those write switches belong in `format:fix` / `lint:fix` — two small helper scripts, not in the required seven, that only `fix` is allowed to call.
A minimal `package.json` that reads as `ready` once gennady is installed — real `lint`, the rest stubbed until the infra flow locks real tools (point `lint` at the project's own source dirs): ```json { "scripts": { "type-check": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (type-check — tsc --noEmit)' >&2", "test": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (test runner)' >&2", "test:coverage": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (coverage)' >&2", "lint": "gennady lint src/", "format": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (formatter, read-only check)' >&2", "format:fix": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (formatter, write mode)' >&2", "lint:fix": "echo 'TODO: настроить инфраструктуру (linter autofix)' >&2", "check": "npm run type-check && npm test && npm run lint && npm run format", "fix": "npm run format:fix && npm run lint:fix && npm run check" } } ``` `lint` may reach `gennady` directly or through an `npm run ` chain — either satisfies the `lint→gennady` check. The leaf stubs print a warning to stderr but **exit 0 — by design they pass**, and chaining them through `check`/`fix` stays read-only-clean since a stub has no `--fix` / `--write` switch to leak — so the gate stays green while the warning keeps the gap visible until the infra flow replaces the stubs with real commands.
SddReadiness.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (`AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🧰 SETUP_R · package.json= · ready=`. Breadcrumb milestones (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Assess · Plan · Apply · Ready.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — an italic blockquote (`> _…_`), 2–3 sentences max: the task retold in the agent's own words plus the single riskiest assumption, linked by wording to the question that resolves it; never a restate of already-settled content — only what is NEW or could be misread (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; if the decision is a flow (data moving, state transitions, start/stop conditions), add a small ASCII diagram — the one place a fenced block is allowed in this message, at most one per message ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` (full format with worked examples lives in `QUESTION_FORMAT`, in the interview / vision directives) ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👷 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.
